section_summary: This section documents Allied efforts to inspect, inventory, microfilm, and determine the ultimate disposition of former Japanese diplomatic and consular archives and official property worldwide following World War II. It contains detailed inventories and reports on Japanese consular archives held in Canada (Vancouver) and New Zealand (Wellington), as well as records from missions in Rome, the Holy See, Argentina, the Netherlands (Curaçao), China, and Colombia. The correspondence also addresses the survey of central government archives in Tokyo and diplomatic negotiations with the Soviet Union regarding the proceeds from the liquidation of Japanese diplomatic properties abroad and access to central archives in Japan.

subfiles.about: Reports on the joint United States-Canadian examination of fifteen boxes of Japanese consular archives recovered from Vancouver, enclosing a detailed inventory and list of extracted files.
subfiles.from: Lewis Clark, Counselor of Embassy, American Embassy, Ottawa
subfiles.summary: Reports on the examination in Ottawa of fifteen boxes of Japanese consular archives recovered from Vancouver, finding mostly routine records but extracting several items on propaganda, Japanese associations, and surveillance for microfilming in Washington. Enclosure 1 provides a comprehensive 21-page inventory of the contents of boxes 5 through 19. Enclosure 2 lists specific files extracted from box 6 for reproduction.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4314: Examination of Japanese Consular Archives

subfiles.about: Transmits prints of documents extracted from Japanese consular archives in Canada to War Department G-2.
subfiles.from: Saxton E. Bradford, Assistant Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.summary: Transmits three sets of prints of documents reproduced from the Japanese consular archives in Canada to War Department G-2.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Japanese Consular Archives in Canada
subfiles.to: Colonel Carter W. Clarke, Deputy Director, Intelligence Division, War Department G-2

subfiles.about: Transmits prints of documents extracted from Japanese consular archives in Canada to the Captured Documents Center.
subfiles.from: Saxton E. Bradford, Assistant Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.summary: Transmits one set of prints of documents reproduced from the Japanese consular archives in Canada to the Captured Documents Center.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Japanese Consular Archives in Canada
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel H. St. Clair, Captured Documents Center, War Department

subfiles.about: Instructs the Political Adviser in Tokyo to explore surveying Japanese Foreign Ministry and Greater East Asia Ministry archives.
subfiles.from: William L. Clayton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Requests informal exploration of surveying Japanese Foreign Ministry and Greater East Asia Ministry archives for policy and intelligence research purposes.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 484 to Tokyo regarding Survey of Japanese Archives
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Draft telegram instructing the Political Adviser in Tokyo to explore surveying Japanese Foreign Ministry archives.
subfiles.from: Division of Foreign Activity Correlation and Division of Japanese Affairs
subfiles.summary: Draft text of telegram requesting informal exploration of surveying Japanese Foreign Ministry and Greater East Asia Ministry archives.
subfiles.title: Draft Telegram to Tokyo regarding Survey of Japanese Foreign Ministry Archives
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Inquires whether Japanese archives held in Vatican City should be forwarded to the Department or destroyed locally.
subfiles.from: Franklin C. Gowen, Vatican City
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether routine Japanese archives in Vatican City should be sent to Washington or destroyed locally by Allied officials.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 91 from Vatican City regarding Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Instructs that Japanese archives in Vatican City be preserved and forwarded to the Department for examination and storage.
subfiles.from: William L. Clayton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Instructs that Japanese archives in Vatican City must be preserved intact and suggested forwarding them to Washington for examination.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 49 to Rome regarding Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Archives

subfiles.about: Approves custody transfer of non-official Japanese personal effects in Rome while ordering official property retained.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Approves custody assumption of private non-official Japanese effects by Giulio Dante, requiring official property to remain stored.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. 3275 to Rome regarding Custody of Private Japanese Property

subfiles.about: Reports on the transfer of private Japanese nationals' luggage from the former Japanese Embassy in Rome to Giulio Dante.
subfiles.from: David McK. Key, American Embassy, Rome
subfiles.summary: Reports that private Japanese effects stored in the former embassy were transferred to Giulio Dante by agreement among the four Allied embassies.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-927 from Rome regarding Custody of Private Japanese Property

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Airgram A-927 regarding private Japanese property in Rome.
subfiles.from: David McK. Key, American Embassy, Rome
subfiles.summary: Duplicate action copy of airgram reporting the transfer of private Japanese effects in Rome to Giulio Dante.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-927 from Rome regarding Custody of Private Japanese Property (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Reports on British requests for Japanese publications and inquires if the Library of Congress desires wartime Italian newspapers.
subfiles.from: David McK. Key, Rome
subfiles.summary: Requests instructions on publications desired from the Japanese Embassy and asks if the Library of Congress wants wartime Italian newspaper files.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 3879 from Rome regarding Italian Newspaper Files and Publications

subfiles.about: States the Library of Congress desires wartime Italian newspaper files if obtainable without cost.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Informs the Embassy that the Library of Congress desires the 1939-1943 newspaper files if free of cost.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1839 to Rome regarding Newspaper Files for Library of Congress

subfiles.about: Reports Chinese Government agreement to proposed measures regarding Japanese consular archives and property in China.
subfiles.from: J. Leighton Stuart, Nanking
subfiles.summary: Confirms Chinese Government agreement to proposed measures regarding Japanese consular archives and property.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1536 from Nanking regarding Japanese Consular Archives and Property

subfiles.about: Reports on the screening, war crimes trial use, and shipment to Washington of Japanese Foreign Ministry archives.
subfiles.from: George Atcheson, Jr., Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports Japanese Foreign Ministry archives were screened and transferred to the International Prosecution Section or Washington Document Center, advising against sending an officer.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 428 from Tokyo regarding Japanese Foreign Ministry Archives

subfiles.about: Transmits twenty-seven packages of archives from the former Japanese Embassy in Argentina to the Department of State.
subfiles.from: R. Kenneth Oakley, Second Secretary of Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.summary: Transmits twenty-seven packages of non-confidential archives from the former Japanese Embassy in Argentina for study and availability to the Four Powers.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 891: Transmitting Certain Archives from the Former Japanese Embassy in Argentina

subfiles.about: Discusses policy regarding diplomatic and consular archives and argues against viewing them purely as intelligence material.
subfiles.from: Albert E. Clattenburg, Jr., Special Projects Division
subfiles.summary: Emphasizes that diplomatic archives constitute vital historical and public records indicating civil rights, rather than merely expendable intelligence material.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Preservation and Purpose of Diplomatic and Consular Archives
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation

subfiles.about: Reports that no archives of the former Japanese Consulate at Winnipeg are in existence.
subfiles.from: Lewis Clark, Counselor of Embassy, Ottawa
subfiles.summary: Confirms Canadian External Affairs found no records of the former Winnipeg consulate exist, correcting an earlier misunderstanding.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4408: Examination of Japanese Consular Archives

subfiles.about: Reports on the examination of Japanese consular archives in Wellington and summarizes the contents of cabinets and a suitcase.
subfiles.from: Elvin Seibert, Second Secretary of Legation, Wellington
subfiles.summary: Reports on inspection of thirty-three boxes and file cabinets of Japanese consular records in Wellington, noting confidential files were destroyed prior to internment.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 446: Examination of Japanese Consular Archives held by New Zealand Government

subfiles.about: Reports on quadripartite committee deliberations in Rome regarding Japanese Embassy publications, newspaper files, and archive disposal.
subfiles.from: David McK. Key, Rome
subfiles.summary: Reports Allied committee agreement in Rome that the Library of Congress may have newspaper files without cost and requests archive instructions.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 3970 from Rome regarding Liquidation of Japanese Embassy Property and Archives

subfiles.about: Instructs that specific Japanese Embassy records in Rome be microfilmed and original archives preserved intact.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Directs microfilming of specified Japanese records in Rome, ordering original archives preserved and storage met from trust funds.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1970 to Rome regarding Microfilming and Preservation of Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Reports transmission of existing archives of the former Japanese Diplomatic Mission to the Holy See with an inventory list.
subfiles.from: Franklin C. Gowen, Assistant to Myron C. Taylor, Vatican City
subfiles.summary: Transmits by sea pouch the remaining archives of the Japanese Mission to the Holy See, enclosing an inventory of accounting books and telegrams.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 550: Archives of Former Japanese Diplomatic Mission to the Holy See

subfiles.about: Notice certifying the replacement of a missing action copy for central file 894.414/11-646.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Designates white copy as permanent record copy replacing unreturned yellow action copy for file 894.414/11-646.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Notice for File 894.414/11-646

subfiles.about: Reports Chinese Foreign Office willingness to assist should SCAP or Japanese agencies need access to consular archives in China.
subfiles.from: J. Leighton Stuart, Nanking
subfiles.summary: Transmits Chinese Foreign Office statement of readiness to render assistance if SCAP or Japanese agencies need consular files in China.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1825 from Nanking regarding Access to Japanese Consular Archives in China (Information Copy)

subfiles.about: Action copy of telegram reporting Chinese Foreign Office willingness to assist with Japanese consular archives in China.
subfiles.from: J. Leighton Stuart, Nanking
subfiles.summary: Action copy of telegram confirming Chinese readiness to assist SCAP or Japanese agencies needing consular files in China.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1825 from Nanking regarding Access to Japanese Consular Archives in China (Action Copy)

subfiles.about: Transmits Netherlands diplomatic note stating that the only Japanese archives held are routine records from Curaçao.
subfiles.from: C. Webb Benton, Counselor of Embassy, American Embassy, The Hague
subfiles.summary: Transmits Netherlands Foreign Ministry note and British Ambassador's cover letter confirming that only routine records from the honorary consul in Curaçao were found.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1242: Examination of Japanese Archives in Possession of Netherlands Government

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy Moscow to stimulate expeditious action from the Soviet Foreign Office regarding Japanese property proposals.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Urges Embassy Moscow to prompt the Soviet Government for concurrence on Japanese diplomatic property and archive proposals.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2182 to Moscow regarding Soviet Concurrence on Japanese Property Proposals

subfiles.about: Reports British Foreign Office agreement to sell official Japanese property when necessary, awaiting Chinese and Soviet concurrence.
subfiles.from: Waldemar J. Gallman, American Embassy, London
subfiles.summary: Reports British Foreign Office agrees to sale of official property where necessary, but withholds field instructions pending Chinese and Soviet concurrence.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-1702 from London regarding British Position on Japanese Property and Archives

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of airgram reporting British position on the disposal of Japanese property and archives.
subfiles.from: Waldemar J. Gallman, American Embassy, London
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of airgram concerning British Foreign Office views on Japanese property sales and Four-Power agreement.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-1702 from London regarding British Position on Japanese Property and Archives (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Transmits correspondence with the Chinese Legation in Havana regarding Japanese Legation property and archives in Bogotá.
subfiles.from: Thomas H. Lockett, Counselor of Embassy, American Embassy, Bogotá
subfiles.summary: Transmits inquiry from Chinese Chargé d'Affaires in Havana and Embassy's reply detailing property sales and joint custody of archives in Bogotá.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2079: Japanese Archives and Properties

subfiles.about: Reports sending a letter to Soviet Deputy Foreign Minister Vyshinsky requesting early indication of the Soviet attitude.
subfiles.from: Walter Bedell Smith, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Reports a letter was sent to Vyshinsky requesting an early indication of Soviet attitude toward Japanese property and archives.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 4487 from Moscow regarding Note to Vyshinski on Japanese Property

subfiles.about: Transmits copy of Ambassador Smith's letter to Soviet Deputy Foreign Minister Vyshinsky concerning Japanese archives and property.
subfiles.from: Walter Bedell Smith, American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet transmitting Ambassador Smith's letter to Vyshinsky urging Soviet reaction to Allied proposals on Japanese property and archives.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Letter to Vyshinski regarding Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Property and Archives

subfiles.about: Notice certifying the replacement of a missing action copy for central file 894.414/12-2846.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Designates white copy as permanent record copy replacing unreturned yellow action copy for file 894.414/12-2846.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Notice for File 894.414/12-2846

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of telegram reporting transmission of letter to Vyshinsky regarding Japanese property proposals.
subfiles.from: Walter Bedell Smith, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of telegram reporting letter sent to Vyshinsky requesting Soviet reaction on Japanese property proposals.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 4487 from Moscow regarding Note to Vyshinski on Japanese Property (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Records discussion on establishing a Japanese Foreign Office project and investigating archives available in Washington and Tokyo.
subfiles.from: H. H. Gosho, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.summary: Records Dr. Noble's interest in initiating a Japanese Foreign Office research project and examining available archives in Washington and Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Interest in Establishing Japanese Foreign Office Project
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research

subfiles.about: Notice certifying that Telegram No. 23 of January 5, 1947 from Moscow was withdrawn due to security classification.
subfiles.from: National Archives and Records Service
subfiles.summary: Notice indicating Telegram No. 23 of January 5, 1947 was withdrawn from file 894.414/1-547 due to security classification.
subfiles.title: Withdrawal Notice for Telegram No. 23 from Moscow

subfiles.about: Corrected copy reporting Soviet conditional acceptance of overseas property disposal and demanding access to central archives in Japan.
subfiles.from: Walter Bedell Smith, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Reports Soviet agreement in principle to overseas property disposal into joint Allied accounts, demanding equal access to central Japanese archives in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 23 from Moscow regarding Soviet Reply on Japanese Archives (Corrected Copy)

subfiles.about: Superseded copy of telegram reporting Soviet reply on overseas property disposal and central archives in Japan.
subfiles.from: Walter Bedell Smith, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Superseded version of telegram reporting Vyshinsky's response accepting overseas property disposal with revisions and requesting central archive access.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 23 from Moscow regarding Soviet Reply on Japanese Archives (Superseded Copy)

subfiles.about: Notice certifying the replacement of a missing action copy for central file 894.414/1-547.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Designates white copy as permanent record copy replacing unreturned yellow action copy for file 894.414/1-547.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Notice for File 894.414/1-547

subfiles.about: Information copy of telegram reporting Soviet conditional acceptance of overseas property disposal and demand for archive access in Japan.
subfiles.from: Walter Bedell Smith, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Information copy of telegram transmitting Vyshinsky's letter on overseas Japanese property proceeds and four-power access to central archives.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 23 from Moscow regarding Soviet Reply on Japanese Archives (Information Copy)

subfiles.about: Requests clarification from Embassy Moscow regarding paragraph numbering in the Soviet reply and states archive demands are being studied.
subfiles.from: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Requests clarification regarding points in the Soviet note and states the demand for access to central archives is being studied.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 101 to Moscow regarding Clarification of Soviet Reply
